doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

chapter: The blues and the jazz economy
title: Defining the blues and Vonnegut's quote
summary: Blue defines the blues as an expression of life experience and agrees with Vonnegut that the blues is the American gift to the world.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: All right. Let’s talk about the blues. Do you have a definition of your own, maybe I want to borrow it. In about a week I’m doing a little presentation about the blues for some group and I often struggle with a succinct but accurate definition of the blues.
A succinct and accurate definition of the blues.
Yeah I think that’s all I could give you.

Yeah. That’s nice of you. The blues, it’s — the blues is it’s an expression of your life experience. And that’s really as simple as I could put it. It’s an expression. Now you could put that in any genre or whatever, but since we’re talking about blues it’s an expression of your life experience. And it can pinpoint the joy, the humility, or even some sadness that you may be experiencing or have experienced that’s made a mark on you, it touches — it reflects your spirit in the purest sense. It really does. Because all of the — because for me I find the blues in all this stuff you know, and playing jazz and playing American music I can hear and find the blues in all of it, there’s an element of it. And as a player it works, it works in the different genres of American music. It’s in there where you find that flat third or that raised fourth or flatted fifth, where and how it’s placed you know, that’s where we speak.

Well said. I wanted to share something I read recently and this is the first opportunity I’ve had to share it. This is from Kurt Vonnegut from his last book, A Man Without a Country and I’m only slightly paraphrasing here. Kurt said “I really like Strauss and Mozart and all that, but the priceless gift that African-Americans gave the whole world was a gift so great that it is now almost the only reason many foreigners still like us. All pop music today: jazz, swing, bebop, Elvis Presley, the Beatles, the Stones, rock & roll, hip-hop and on and on is derived from the blues.”

Yeah. It’s the American experience. The blues is the American experience. Now blues didn’t originate in America. Blues came over from Africa. Okay? I don’t know if you’ve had the opportunity or experience to hear some of the, you know, some of the music in Africa that depicts that sound, but it’s there man. I’ve heard it. And the way it developed here is uniqueness. That’s our culture you know. That’s American culture. And I agree with what he said, this is something that has permeated and touched the rest of the world and I believe that despite what others say or think I believe that the rest of the world has a great appreciation for us because of the blues. It’s touched everybody because they can’t play what they call jazz without touching the blues either, and this is a music that is just — we’ve shared it with the world. You know? And I agree, it’s one of the reasons, it gives them a reason to like us. Yeah. Everywhere I go, anywhere I go, and this has been in any country that I’ve been in we’re treated differently, we’re treated respectfully
